You are planning a short narrated movie (story-id "s1").

Narrative to adapt:
A courier carries a sealed letter across a rainy harbour town.

How this movie is made: it is ONE continuous take, built 6 seconds at a time. Panel 1 starts from a single still picture, and every later panel continues from the exact last frame of the panel before it. There are no cuts and no jumps in time or place: a new place, object or character must arrive through visible movement inside a beat.

Write the story bible as one JSON object with exactly these seven keys:

title: the movie's title, at most 8 words.
logline: one sentence of 8 to 40 words that summarises the story.
cast: a list with one object per individual character who acts or speaks on screen, with the keys id, phrase and descriptor; a group of people (a crowd, an audience, fans, spectators, a team) is never a cast entry, and belongs in the setting sentence of its place. id is c1, c2, c3 and so on, in order. phrase is the character's referring phrase: at most four words, built only from details in their descriptor or stated by the narrative; the movie names them by this exact phrase everywhere. descriptor is their full visual description in 8 to 60 words that starts with "a " or "an " and does not end with a full stop: apparent age group, build, skin tone, hair colour, length and style, clothing and accessories. The following characters are already cast; list them first in cast with exactly these ids, phrases and descriptors, and give your own characters the next ids. Every one of them is in this movie: put each one's id in the cast of at least one beat. When the narrative calls one of them by their name, it means that character, whom the movie names only by their phrase:
- id c1, name "kyra", phrase "the woman in grey", descriptor "a young woman with long black hair pinned up with jade hairpins wearing a grey kimono"
- id c2, name "ronin", phrase "the ronin", descriptor "a lean man in his late thirties with a topknot and a scarred brow wearing an indigo haori"
locations: a list with one object per place, with the keys id and setting. id is l1, l2 and so on. setting is one sentence of 12 to 45 words that starts with "The setting is" and names the period, the place, the ground, the light and any crowd or other group of people in the background.
props: a list with one object per object that matters to the story, with the keys id and name. id is p1, p2 and so on; name is a short noun phrase for the object. Use an empty list when no object matters.
beats: a list of 3 to 5 objects, one per panel in order, with the keys index, arc, action, shot, camera, location, cast and speaker. index runs from 1 to the number of beats. This movie's target length is 3 beats, and like a word range it is soft: use 3 beats when the narrative fits them, and add a beat, up to 5 beats in all, only for something the narrative needs that no other beat can hold. arc is one of introduction, rising, climax, falling, resolution, in story order; the first beat is introduction, the last is resolution, and at least one beat is climax. action is one sentence of 6 to 40 words saying what the characters physically do during these 6 seconds: one continuous physical action that a camera can film, not a sequence of steps, with no on-screen text. shot is exactly one of: extreme wide shot, wide shot, medium shot, medium close-up, close-up, extreme close-up. camera is exactly one of: slow push-in, slow pull-back, tracking, handheld, slow pan left, slow pan right, slow tilt up, slow tilt down, static. Give every beat one camera move from this list, and use static only for a deliberate hold: at most one beat in three may be static, so at most 1 in this movie. On a beat with a speaker, prefer slow push-in, slow pull-back, tracking or handheld, and never use a pan or a tilt, which sweeps the speaker's face out of the frame. location is the id of the place where the beat happens. cast is the list of ids of the characters on screen in the beat, at most 4. speaker is the id of the one character who says something aloud on screen during the beat, or an empty string when nobody speaks; give a speaker only where a spoken line moves the story. A beat with a speaker shows that character facing the camera, in a medium shot, medium close-up or close-up; its cast is the speaker's id plus the id of every already-cast character who is still in frame and stays silent, and no character of your own. The speaker may move during the beat, as long as their face stays in frame and lit while they speak. Write a speaking beat's action as what the speaker physically does, never as speaking, and end it with the speaker still in frame: nobody else acts after the line, and when the narrative has the speaker leave, or another character act, after a line, give that a later beat with no speaker, adding that beat when the beat count allows it, and leave it out only when it does not.
loras: an object with the keys global, per_beat and stills, each empty: global and stills are empty lists and per_beat is an empty object.

Rules for this movie: keep consecutive beats at the same location unless the action itself moves the characters there, and put every character who can be seen in the opening frame in beat 1's cast.

Reply with the JSON object only, with no text before or after it. Do not call any tool: do NOT read any file, do NOT run run_python or any other tool to check it, and do NOT count or recount words.
